articles.title: Jesse Eisenberg Says Fans Aren’t Crazy With Him Because ‘There’s No Sexuality to My Work’: Life Is ‘Different’ When People ‘Want to Sleep With’ You
articles.summary: Jesse Eisenberg recently told the New Yorker that fans of his are “mostly fine” when he’s in public, a fact he attributes to his generally sexless resume. “People are mostly fine,” he said to reporter Rachel Syme when asked if strangers ever interrupt him when they spot him working on scripts.
body: Though, despite Eisenberg’s assertion, his “Fleishman Is in Trouble” co-star Claire Danes told Syme that people began to “rubberneck” when the two had a coincidental run-in on the street and stopped to chat. “People are very aware of him as a figure, even though he is so determined to be invisible,” she said.

Elsewhere in the lengthy profile, Aaron Sorkin, who directed Eisenberg as a young Mark Zuckerberg in “The Social Network,” told the outlet that “I hardly know him at all,” noting that the actor reminds “me of Holden Caulfield, if that makes any sense. He has absolutely no patience for phonies.”

Eisenberg earned an Oscar nomination for the part, but has since been outspoken about his decision not to reprise the role in the director’s follow-up, “ The Social Reckoning,” released earlier this year. “I’d be out at a bar, and a drunk guy would say, ‘Hey, I love your website,’” he told the New Yorker. “And as I’m pretending to laugh, I’d just wish all of the oxygen would leave my lungs, and that I would collapse on the floor in front of this guy and show him what he’s doing to me.”

articles.title: ‘South Park’ Season 29 Finale: ‘GTA 6’ Inspires Stan, Kyle and Cartman to Get to the Bottom of South America’s Power Outages
articles.summary: In the sixth and final episode of “South Park” Season 29, South America has once again been hit with major power outages — but this time it’s serious, considering “Grand Theft Auto VI” has finally been released, which means the residents of the mountain town will stop at nothing to restore their…
body: The town’s politicians have no idea what to do about the issue, but luckily for them, a group of angry townspeople barge into South American City Hall and proclaim they know who’s behind the outages: the Chinese. More specifically, the outages are the result of Chinese cyberattacks. Relieved, the town’s politicians let them believe this is the case — “Yes, you figured it out. It’s definitely cyber attacks by the Chinese” — as they begin to search for a Chinese spy who must be living in South America.

But Butters has known the billionaires were to blame since the beginning, and confides in Stan, Kyle and Cartman. Oh, and a zombified Kenny (who got blown up by an e-bike during the season’s premiere) also makes a few appearances. Turns out, Kenny’s spirit can’t move on until the group figures out what’s going on and exposes all the corruption in South America — great timing for them, as they’ve all learned about the data centers and are ready to make a change. The gang takes this revelation to City Hall, where the politicians explain how it all began “with those damn e-bikes” and fear that the group of kids is going to blow their secret deal with the billionaires.

articles.title: U2 Salutes Dolly Parton With Recreation of Their ‘Torn’ Duet in NFL Thanksgiving Eve Halftime Show
articles.summary: U2 paid tribute to Dolly Parton as part of its halftime performance Wednesday night at the NFL’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game. The “duet” between a live Bono and a recording of Parton from last summer was the centerpiece of a highly promoted 10-minute set between halves of the contest between…
body: U2 did not attempt to cram as many songs into their brief performance as other superstars have during halftime performances, getting in four. The band opened with an abridged “Sunday Bloody Sunday” and ended with “”Pride (in the Name of Love)” and Where the Streets Have No Name” — only squeezing in one song from their new album, the Parton duet, “Torn,” with images of Dolly projected onto three huge curtains that dropped around their stage at the 50-yard line.

About a hundred extras took part in the performances — forming not a marching band, but a marching choir. U2 was also joined by the Womack Sisters, a vocal trio that has just been nominated for best new artist at the Grammys.

The four key songs were just condensed enough that U2’s members were actually able to use part of their allotted 10 minutes walking to the stage at the beginning and walking back out through the assembled marchers at the end, in casual yet dramatic fashion.

articles.title: Microdrama Revenue to Hit $20 Billion in 2026, but Profits Outside China Remain Thin, Media Partners Asia Report Finds
articles.summary: Global microdrama revenue will climb 24% to $20 billion in 2026, but outside China the business has yet to prove it can make reliable money, according to new research from Media Partners Asia.
body: China still dominates. The country will generate $15.2 billion this year, or 76% of the global total, after revenue jumped 90% in 2025. MPA expects growth there to cool to 6.7% annually as viewing levels off, taking Chinese revenue to $21 billion by 2031. The firm’s China figure is narrower than the National Radio and Television Administration’s RMB100 billion ($15 billion) estimate for 2025, which also counts producer outlays on AI models and platform investment.

Free, ad-supported viewing overtook paid viewing in China in 2025. Advertising will make up 69% of the country’s microdrama revenue this year and 79% by 2031. ByteDance, which operates Hongguo and Douyin, takes 56% of Chinese revenue, and ByteDance, Tencent and Kuaishou together command 82%.

Dedicated apps outside China will earn $4.87 billion in 2026, a third more than last year, with MPA forecasting $11 billion by 2031 on annual growth of 17.7%. The U.S. remains the biggest single market at $1.71 billion, though that is 2% lower than in 2025. Asia-Pacific excluding China, at $1.44 billion, is set to overtake the U.S. in 2029.
points: Global microdrama revenue will climb 24% to $20 billion in 2026, but outside China the business has yet to prove it can make reliable money, according to new research from Media Partners Asia.

articles.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies aged 65
articles.summary: The musician, who co-wrote some of the band's biggest hits, had been treated for prostate cancer.
body: Andy Taylor, the guitarist for the pop group Duran Duran, has died at the age of 65.
Born in Tynemouth, he co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits, including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film; and also worked with artists like Robert Palmer, Rod Stewart and Belinda Carlisle.
In a statement, his bandmates said Taylor had fought "a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer" and "passed away peacefully at home, surrounded by his family, on Monday 23 November".
His wife, Tracey, said the musician "was the rock of our family", adding: "We will miss him every single day".

articles.title: BBC launches partnership with Met Office for weather coverage
articles.summary: The corporation says the deal will deliver more regional, digital and 10-day forecasts to audiences.
body: The BBC has said it will offer more regional, digital and 10-day weather forecasts under a new partnership with the Met Office, which begins on Thursday.
The collaboration, announced last year, aims to bring together the Met Office's weather and climate intelligence with the BBC's journalism and reach, the broadcaster said.
Director general Matt Brittin said the partnership would mean "serving our audiences with the most accurate, reliable and helpful weather service we can".
But the launch comes during a savings drive at the corporation, which has seen some other weather services and bulletins dropped as part of wider cuts.

articles.title: ‘South Park’ Season Finale Drops Kenny Into ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ as South America Comes Clean
articles.summary: Power outages, penis billionaires and an undead Kenny collide as the season ties up (most of) its loose ends.
body: All is not well in South America (née South Park ) in the season 29 finale. The long-anticipated November release of Grand Theft Auto VI — the show’s metaphorical stand-in for the midterm elections — has finally arrived, but rolling power outages caused by local billionaires’ AI-powered data centers are keeping the townspeople — from the little-seen Goth Kids to Mr. Garrison to Big Gay Al, and of course, our core boy heroes — from enjoying the biggest media release of all time.

For an episode that packs plenty in, calling back to much of the season’s action and picking up most of the plot threads it introduced (minus, unfortunately, the great Tweek and Craig ), it’s Lu Kim, the Asian American owner of City Wok and now City Ending massage, who walks away with the heaviest storyline. He’s quickly scapegoated and placed under suspicious watch by armed South America residents, who are made aware of a Chinese spy that feels a little like a recent international tech world scandal. A Shitty Ending feels inevitable.

articles.title: Andy Taylor: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a true Wild Boy
articles.summary: How a wayward child from the north-east of England made it with the world's biggest band.
body: Andy Taylor, who has died aged 65, was the wild boy of Duran Duran.
In the early 1980s, the pop legends sold over 100 million records and dominated the charts in both Britain and the United States.
But success came at a cost. For Taylor, global superstardom became a cocaine and alcohol fuelled nightmare that left him burnt out and battling clinical depression.
"For sure, we paraded around in our fast cars with beautiful models on yachts in the south of France without needing to pay the bill," he later wrote.

articles.title: UK Town of Culture bid withdrawn in Strabane after it causes 'great division'
articles.summary: The County Tyrone town was shortlisted as one of 15 possible locations for the inaugural UK Town of Culture 2028, with the chance to win £3m.
body: A competition that is supposed to celebrate local towns has been rejected by a council after it caused "great division" over its UK title.
However, the local council voted not to go ahead with the bid on Wednesday with one councillor claiming it "has the potential to be a disaster for Strabane - for community relations".
The motion, which was put forward by independent councillors, was backed by the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) and Sinn Féin.

A report prepared for councillors said that money had come from a £60,000 Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) grant, and would need to be repaid if the bid did not make it to the final submission stage.

articles.title: The Cliff Booth Movie Brings Back Two Key Characters From Once Upon A Time In Hollywood
articles.summary: In addition to Brad Pitt's Cliff Booth, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth brings back a couple more familiar faces from Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.
body: "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is not a direct sequel to "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," as we knew from Quentin Tarantino handing over the director's chair to David Fincher. But still, you had to wonder if any other familiar faces would pop up in this new mis-adventure.

Part of the appeal of returning to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" is that the movie ended by changing history. Thanks to the actions of Cliff, actress Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie) is not murdered by the Manson family. How does the entertainment world and Los Angeles change by 1977, when "Cliff Booth" takes place, because of that ripple effect? Tarantino wrote the script for "Cliff Booth," and if any filmmaker is equipped to dig into the nitty-gritty of such a change in Hollywood history, down to the most obscure B-pictures and forgotten TV, it's him.
